questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with a painless genital ulcer with indurated margins. Dark-field microscopy of the exudate shows motile spirochetes. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is caused by Treponema pallidum. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose is the treatment of choice. The painless indurated ulcer and dark-field microscopy findings are classic for primary syphilis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer from Bihar presents with hypopigmented patches on the trunk with loss of sensation. Slit-skin smear shows 3+ bacillary index. Which type of leprosy is this most consistent with?
questions.exp: High bacillary index (3+ or more) indicates lepromatous leprosy. Lepromatous leprosy has high bacterial load, poor cell-mediated immunity, and multiple lesions. BI of 4-6+ is typically seen in lepromatous leprosy.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops tense bullae on normal-appearing skin, predominantly on the flexural areas. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae on normal or erythematous skin, with flexural predilection in elderly. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. The target antigen is BPAG2 (BP180) and BPAG1 (BP230).

questions.q: A 30-year-old male with HIV presents with multiple verrucous plaques on the perianal region. Biopsy shows koilocytes and hyperkeratosis. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: HPV type 16 (and 18) are high-risk oncogenic types associated with anogenital carcinoma, especially in immunocompromised patients. HPV 6 and 11 are low-risk types causing condyloma acuminata. In HIV patients, high-risk HPV types are more likely to cause transformation.

questions.q: A 20-year-old student presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales on the scalp and elbows. Auspitz sign is positive. Which histological finding is pathognomonic of this condition?
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses (neutrophil collections in stratum corneum) are pathognomonic of psoriasis. Spongiform pustules of Kogoj in spinous layer are also characteristic. The clinical picture describes psoriasis vulgaris.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with facial butterfly rash, joint pain, and photosensitivity for 3 months. ANA is 1:640 with anti-dsDNA positive. Which cutaneous finding is most specific for SLE?
questions.exp: Discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE) is the most specific cutaneous manifestation of lupus. It shows scarring, follicular plugging, and atrophy. While malar rash is more sensitive, DLE is more specific for lupus.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman on methotrexate for psoriasis develops megaloblastic anemia. The mechanism of methotrexate action in psoriasis is:
questions.exp: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), thereby reducing folate availability for DNA synthesis. This reduces keratinocyte proliferation in psoriasis. Supplementation with folic acid reduces side effects like megaloblastic anemia.

questions.q: A neonate develops widespread blistering within 48 hours of birth. The bullae are flaccid and Nikolsky sign is positive. Blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) in neonates is caused by exfoliative toxins (ETs) of S. aureus phage group II. It produces widespread superficial blistering with positive Nikolsky sign. The split is at the granular layer due to ET-A and ET-B cleaving desmoglein 1.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male traveler returns from Southeast Asia with annular scaling plaques on the trunk. KOH examination shows 'spaghetti and meatball' appearance. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.exp: The 'spaghetti and meatball' appearance on KOH is pathognomonic of Malassezia furfur (pityriasis versicolor). Oral itraconazole 200mg for 7 days is effective for extensive cases. The short-chain fatty acids produced by Malassezia inhibit melanogenesis causing hypopigmentation.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male smoker presents with a pearly nodule with telangiectatic vessels on the nose. It has been slowly enlarging for 2 years. Dermoscopy shows arborizing vessels. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) classically presents as a pearly/translucent nodule with rolled borders and telangiectasia on sun-exposed areas. Dermoscopy showing arborizing (tree-like) vessels is characteristic. BCC is the most common skin cancer and rarely metastasizes.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman develops painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the right T4 dermatome. She had chickenpox at age 5. The antiviral treatment should be initiated within:
questions.exp: Herpes zoster (shingles) is caused by reactivation of VZV. Oral antivirals (acyclovir, valacyclovir, famciclovir) should be started within 72 hours of onset to reduce severity and duration, and to prevent postherpetic neuralgia. The dermatomal distribution is characteristic.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with hyperpigmented macules and papules on the trunk following a febrile illness. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. The specific antigen targeted in this viral infection is:
questions.exp: VZV uses glycoprotein gE (and gI) for cell-to-cell spread and immune evasion. The Tzanck smear showing multinucleated giant cells confirms varicella/herpes. Desmoglein 1 and 3 are targets in pemphigus; Collagen XVII (BP180) is targeted in bullous pemphigoid.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT-MB develops sudden onset tender erythematous nodules on the face and trunk with fever and joint pain. What is the most likely reaction and its treatment?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL/Type 2 reaction) occurs in BL and LL leprosy. It presents with tender erythematous nodules, fever, and systemic features. Thalidomide is the drug of choice (100-400mg/day) due to its anti-TNF-alpha activity. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Prednisolone is an alternative.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops 'swan-neck' deformity of fingers, Raynaud's phenomenon, and telangiectasia on the face. Skin biopsy shows thickened dermis with increased collagen. What is the specific autoantibody associated with diffuse systemic sclerosis?
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibody is associated with diffuse systemic sclerosis and predicts pulmonary fibrosis. Anti-centromere antibodies are associated with limited systemic sclerosis (CREST syndrome). Anti-Ro/SSA is for Sjögren's syndrome; anti-Jo-1 for dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with painful genital ulcers that are soft and irregular with undermined edges. Inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo) is present. Gram stain of pus shows 'school of fish' pattern. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi. It presents with soft, painful genital ulcers with irregular undermined edges (unlike the hard, painless chancre of syphilis). Gram stain shows gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' or 'railroad track' arrangement. Treatment is azithromycin 1g single dose or ceftriaxone 250mg IM.

questions.q: During a Mohs micrographic surgery, the surgeon excises tissue in horizontal layers. This technique is primarily used for:
opts: High-risk BCC at critical anatomical sites
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery achieves the highest cure rates (99% for primary BCC) by examining 100% of surgical margins using horizontal frozen sections. It is indicated for high-risk BCC (recurrent, large, poorly defined margins) at critical sites (nose, eyelid, ear, lips) where tissue conservation is important.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman with vitiligo affecting 20% BSA desires repigmentation. The pathophysiology involves destruction of melanocytes by:
opts: Autoreactive CD8+ T cells targeting melanocyte-specific antigens
questions.exp: Vitiligo is an autoimmune disorder where CD8+ cytotoxic T cells recognize melanocyte-specific antigens (tyrosinase, MART-1, gp100) and destroy melanocytes. The JAK-STAT pathway (IFN-γ/CXCL10) is a key pathogenic mechanism. JAK inhibitors (ruxolitinib) are now approved for treatment.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with erosions in the mouth for 3 months followed by skin blisters. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposits in a 'chicken wire' pattern. The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets desmoglein 3 (mucosal dominant - oral lesions) and desmoglein 1 (epidermal dominant - skin lesions). DIF shows intercellular IgG in an epithelial 'chicken wire' or 'fishnet' pattern. Positive Nikolsky sign is due to acantholysis above the basal layer.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child is brought with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. The most common causative organism in India is:
questions.exp: Impetigo in India is predominantly caused by Staphylococcus aureus (unlike Western countries where Streptococcus pyogenes was common). Honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth are characteristic of non-bullous impetigo. Treatment is topical mupirocin or systemic anti-staphylococcal antibiotics.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male with poorly controlled diabetes presents with rapidly spreading necrotic tissue involving the scrotum and perineum. Crepitus is present. What is the diagnosis and emergency treatment?
opts: Fournier's gangrene - surgical debridement + broad-spectrum antibiotics
Necrotizing fasciitis type II - hyperbaric oxygen only
questions.exp: Fournier's gangrene is a type of necrotizing fasciitis affecting the genitoperineal region, more common in diabetics and immunocompromised. Crepitus indicates gas-forming organisms. Emergency surgical debridement is mandatory with broad-spectrum antibiotics covering gram-positive, gram-negative, and anaerobes. Mortality is high without immediate surgery.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman on oral contraceptive pills develops symmetrical hyperpigmentation on the cheeks, upper lip, and forehead. What is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Triple combination (hydroquinone + tretinoin + moderate potency steroid) + strict sun protection
questions.exp: Melasma (OCP-induced/hormonal) treatment: Kligman's triple combination (hydroquinone 4% + tretinoin 0.025% + fluocinolone acetonide 0.01%) is the gold standard first-line topical treatment combined with strict photoprotection (SPF 30+). Stopping OCPs and sun protection are also important.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male with chronic tinea unguium of all 10 fingernails is prescribed oral terbinafine. The mechanism of action of terbinafine is:
opts: Disruption of fungal cell membrane ergosterol
questions.exp: Terbinafine (allylamine) inhibits squalene epoxidase, leading to accumulation of squalene (toxic to fungi) and deficiency of ergosterol. Azoles inhibit CYP51 (lanosterol demethylase). Polyenes (amphotericin B, nystatin) bind ergosterol. Echinocandins inhibit β-1,3-glucan synthase.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with asymptomatic hypopigmented macules and mild ichthyotic skin since childhood. Peripheral blood smear shows acanthocytes. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Refsum disease (phytanic acid storage disease) presents with ichthyosis, retinitis pigmentosa, peripheral neuropathy, and cerebellar ataxia. Elevated phytanic acid is diagnostic. It is due to deficiency of phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase. Chanarin-Dorfman shows lipid vacuoles in neutrophils; Netherton shows trichorrhexis invaginata.

questions.q: A 35-year-old female develops itchy, erythematous, vesicular eruption on the dorsum of hands and forearms after wearing a metal watch. Patch test is positive to nickel sulfate. This is an example of:
questions.exp: Allergic contact dermatitis is a classic Type IV (cell-mediated, delayed-type) hypersensitivity reaction mediated by sensitized CD4+ T cells (Th1) and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells. It occurs 48-72 hours after re-exposure to the allergen. Nickel is the most common contact allergen worldwide.

questions.q: A 65-year-old woman presents with palpable purpura on the lower legs following an upper respiratory tract infection. Renal biopsy shows IgA deposits. The skin biopsy will most likely show:
opts: Neutrophilic infiltrate with nuclear dust and vessel wall IgA deposits
questions.exp: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura) shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA deposits in vessel walls on DIF. Skin biopsy shows neutrophilic infiltrate with leukocytoclasis (nuclear dust) and fibrinoid necrosis of small vessels. Palpable purpura is the cardinal sign.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male with LGV presents with a groove sign (inguinal groove between inguinal and femoral lymph nodes). The causative organism serovars are:
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2 (most common), and L3. The groove sign (inguinal groove between enlarged inguinal and femoral lymph nodes) is pathognomonic. Serovars D-K cause non-gonococcal urethritis and cervicitis. Treatment is doxycycline 100mg BD for 21 days.

questions.q: During a punch biopsy procedure, a 4mm punch is used. Which layer of skin does the standard punch biopsy routinely include to adequately diagnose a panniculitis?
opts: Epidermis, full dermis, and subcutaneous fat
Epidermis and dermis to papillary layer
questions.exp: For diagnosing panniculitis, the biopsy must include subcutaneous fat. A standard punch biopsy can reach subcutaneous fat if the punch is inserted to its full depth and angled appropriately. Alternatively, an incisional/excisional biopsy is preferred for panniculitis to ensure adequate fat is sampled.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male with longstanding psoriasis develops scaly scalp, plantar keratoderma, and nail changes. He is started on etanercept. The mechanism of action is:
questions.exp: Etanercept is a soluble TNF receptor fusion protein (TNFR2-Fc fusion) that competitively binds TNF-alpha and TNF-beta, preventing them from binding cell surface receptors. Ustekinumab targets IL-12/23. Secukinumab/ixekizumab target IL-17A. Rituximab targets CD20.

questions.q: A 55-year-old female presents with progressive thickening and hyperpigmentation of skin in the axilla and neck with papillomatous surface. She also has a BMI of 38. Blood tests reveal hyperinsulinemia. This condition is most likely:
opts: Acanthosis nigricans associated with insulin resistance
questions.exp: Acanthosis nigricans associated with obesity and insulin resistance is the most common type. Hyperinsulinemia stimulates IGF-1 receptors on keratinocytes causing hyperproliferation. Malignant acanthosis nigricans (associated with internal malignancy) presents acutely with rapid progression and tripe palms.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with progressive dysphagia and calcinosis cutis on the fingers. EMG shows myopathic changes and muscle enzymes are elevated. The pathognomonic skin finding for this condition is:
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis classically presents with heliotrope rash (violaceous periorbital erythema/edema) and Gottron papules (violaceous flat-topped papules over knuckles). Dysphagia indicates pharyngeal muscle involvement. Calcinosis is more common in juvenile DM. Anti-Mi-2 antibodies are specific for DM with classic skin features.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive male with CD4 count of 50 cells/μL presents with deep nodular lesions on the face and trunk. The lesions contain encapsulated yeast forms with narrow-based budding visible on India ink preparation. The most appropriate treatment is:
opts: Amphotericin B deoxycholate induction followed by fluconazole consolidation
questions.exp: Cryptococcosis in immunocompromised patients is caused by Cryptococcus neoformans. India ink shows narrow-based budding encapsulated yeasts. Treatment per IDSA guidelines: induction with amphotericin B deoxycholate (0.7-1mg/kg/day) + flucytosine for 2 weeks, then consolidation with fluconazole 400mg/day for 8 weeks, then maintenance fluconazole 200mg/day.
